Add many input ports for fan-in (#9)

An input port declared "many": true accepts multiple edges and collects
every delivered value in manifest edge order into a list. Guards compose:
a guarded edge into a many port contributes only when it fires, which is

Task for this repository:

spawn cells: admit and run a manifest delivered as data (#22)

An upstream cell (typically an agent emitting json) produces an organism
manifest on the manifest port; spawn parses it through the ordinary
contract, admits it to the store, compiles it, and runs it as a nested
organism under the spawn path. args maps interface inputs; data emits
the interface outputs; digest emits the admitted manifest's sha256 as
provenance.

Generated manifests are data, never code — they resolve against the host
registry and executors, inherit root budgets and depth (each nesting
level consumes one depth step), and replay deterministically since the
manifest rides an edge and putManifest is idempotent. Invalid manifests
fail through normal contract errors, routable via on:fail.

breed example: an agent emits an echo-organism manifest; spawn admits
and runs it; the child's output surfaces through data.

Task for this repository:

Route effects through host-admitted executor capabilities (#11)

Executors now declare which effect kinds they serve and the scheduler
selects only compatible backends. Model executors admit agent and
classifier; decision executors admit classifier and decide; index
executors admit recall; gate approval requires an executor the host
explicitly admitted for it. Undeclared executors default to the
model-generation kinds, so a legacy adapter never silently gains
approval, decision, or index authority.

Selection fails closed in both directions: a named route that cannot
serve the kind records an EFFECT_UNBOUND effect rather than falling
back, and an unrouted request skips incompatible executors entirely.
Scripted fixtures are route wildcards — they simulate any named route
so manifests stay exercisable under deterministic tests — while live
executors never wildcard. Replay resolves by request digest before
capability selection, keeping offline verification independent of
which executors the host currently admits.

The native host mirrors the same matrix, including the scripted
wildcard distinction, and the spec documents effect kinds as the
first capability classes.

Serve a real 404 page with the shared design-kit status page (v0.21.0) (#50)

sys1.io answered a missing page with Vercel's bare `NOT_FOUND` page,
which keeps no one on the site. It now serves `site/404.html` (Vercel
returns it with status 404 for any unmatched path), built from the
shared design-kit v0.21.0 status page.

## What the reader sees
- The site header and footer, as on the docs page.
- **Install Sys1** (`/#install`) as the primary button, the same action
as the homepage hero.
- "Did you mean …?" for a mistyped address, matched against every page
the site serves (`/docs`, `/docs/evaluations`, `/compare`, `/skills`,
and the history pages).
- Three next links:
- Docs: "Install Sys1, pick hosted Jev or a local model, and call it
from Node, Bun, or HTTP."
- Compare models: "JevBench scores, where each model runs, and what your
workload would cost."
- Evaluations: "Sys1’s own tests of each backend, wrong answers and raw
reports included."
- One quiet `/llms.txt` line and the "404" glyph drawn as the design-kit
dot field.

## How it is built
The site has no build step and vendors design-kit files with recorded
digests, so this follows the appearance-bundle pattern:
`scripts/build-site-status-page.ts --refresh <design-kit checkout>
4a5e0b6… v0.21.0` reads `src/status-page.css`, `LICENSE`,
`dist/index.js` and `dist/browser/index.js` from Git objects at the
tagged commit, renders the markup with `renderStatusPageHtml` into
`site/404.html` between markers, bundles `attachStatusPage` into
`site/status-page.js`, and writes
`site/vendor/hraness-status-page/provenance.json`.
`test/site-status-page.test.ts` checks every digest, the page chrome,
and that an edited status region fails.

The site's unlayered element rules for `h1`–`h3`, `p` and links now skip
`.hraness-status-page`, the way they already skip the footer; without
that, the site's display heading sizes overrode the page's layered type.
Other pages are unchanged (same selectors and specificity).

## Evidence
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun test test/site-status-page.test.ts`.
- Real browser (agent-browser) against `site/` served with a 404
fallback: HTTP 404, `data-hraness-status-field="live"` at 1440 and 390
px in light and dark, no horizontal overflow, header and footer present;
`/docs/evaluation` shows "Did you mean Evaluations?".
